title: How to Plan an Iten Running Camp for Your Club, Then Finish on Safari
meta_title: Iten Running Camp Planner for Clubs and Squads
meta_description: Iten running camp planning for clubs: altitude, weekly sessions, flights via Eldoret, rooming, group pricing and a Rift Valley safari to finish.
excerpt: An Iten running camp lets your club train at about 2,400 metres in Kenya's Home of Champions. Here is how to plan the weekly sessions, flights, rooms and a safari to finish.
content:
An Iten running camp gives your club two weeks of training at about 2,400 metres in the Kenyan town that has produced generations of distance champions, on red dirt roads above the Kerio Valley. Most clubs fly Nairobi to Eldoret, stay 10 to 14 days, train with local groups, then rest on a short Rift Valley safari.

The hard part for an organiser is not the running, it is everything around it: flights for twenty people arriving on different days, rooms near the track, a vehicle for Saturday long runs, a plan for the slower runners and a safari that does not wreck anyone's legs. This guide walks through those logistics, the weekly rhythm in Iten and how our club safaris team builds the whole trip around your training block.

Quick Facts

  • Altitude: Iten sits at about 2,400 metres above sea level in Elgeyo-Marakwet County
  • Getting there: Nairobi to Eldoret by air in about 1 hour, then about 35 km by road to Iten
  • Ideal stay: 10 to 14 days of training, plus 2 to 3 days of safari to finish
  • Group size: Comfortable for 6 to 25 runners; bigger squads split across two guesthouses
  • Weekly anchors: Track work on Tuesdays, a big group fartlek on Thursdays, long runs on Saturdays
  • Group pricing: Every 7th place is free for each 6 paying travellers

Why Choose an Iten Running Camp Over Training at Home?

An Iten running camp puts your club in a place built around distance running: soft dirt roads at altitude, hundreds of athletes training at dawn and a culture where early nights and simple food are normal. Runners come home fitter, but most also say the routine itself is the lesson.

Iten is a small town on the edge of the Elgeyo Escarpment, with the Kerio Valley dropping away to the east. St Patrick's High School in the town has produced a long line of famous athletes, from Ibrahim Hussein to David Rudisha, and the "Home of Champions" reputation has drawn foreign runners for decades. You will see runners on every road from about 6am.

For a club, the value of an Iten running camp is shared. A squad that trains together for two weeks in Iten tends to come home with a common language about pacing, recovery and effort. Coaches like it because there is nothing else to do: no commute, no office, just running, eating, stretching and sleeping.

Is altitude training in Iten worth it for amateurs?

Altitude training at an Iten running camp is worth it for amateurs if you treat it as a training holiday rather than a miracle cure. You will feel slower for the first few days, and that is normal. The real gains for club runners come from consistent volume on soft surfaces, group runs at a steady pace and proper rest.

What Does a Training Week in Iten Look Like?

A week at an Iten running camp follows the local rhythm: easy runs most mornings, a track session on Tuesday, a large group fartlek on Thursday and a long run on Saturday, with Sunday as a rest day. Afternoons are for a short second run, core work, massage or sleep.

The public Kamariny Stadium is the town's best-known track, a dirt oval used by groups from early morning. The Thursday fartlek has long started from a junction a few kilometres north of town on the road towards Marakwet, with runners agreeing the on and off pattern on the spot. Saturday long runs are often taken to flatter, slightly lower routes towards Eldoret, which is where a group vehicle earns its keep.

DayMorningAfternoon
MondayEasy 40-60 minutes on dirt roadsCore and stretching
TuesdayTrack session at Kamariny StadiumRest or 20-minute shake-out
WednesdayEasy run, hill stridesKerio Valley viewpoint walk
ThursdayGroup fartlek with local runnersMassage or sleep
FridayEasy runShort second run
SaturdayLong run on a flatter route, by group vehicleRest
SundayRest day, church or market visitTeam meeting and plan for the week

Treat this Iten running camp week as a template, not a rule. In the first week we suggest everyone runs easy, skips the Thursday fartlek or joins only the first half, and keeps the Saturday run short. Week two is when your faster runners can start mixing it with the locals.

Planning an Iten Running Camp for a Club or Squad

Planning an Iten running camp for a club comes down to four things: dates that suit your race calendar, rooms close to the track, flights that land everyone on time and a budget each runner can see. Lock those early and the training takes care of itself.

Our guide to organising a group safari covers deposits and payments step by step, and the wider group safaris section shows every type of trip we run.

How many runners can you take to an Iten running camp?

Groups of 6 to 25 runners fit comfortably, and larger squads can split across two guesthouses in the same part of town. The town's athlete-focused guesthouses and hotels are small, so for 15 or more runners we hold rooms early, especially for popular dates booked months ahead by other visiting runners.

Rooming at an Iten running camp works best in twins, with a few singles for coaches and anyone who snores. Ask runners to send their rooming preferences with their deposit, not the week before departure, because changing a rooming list in a small guesthouse is far harder than in a big hotel.

Flights, arrivals and transfers

Most clubs heading to an Iten running camp fly into Nairobi and connect to Eldoret on a domestic flight of about an hour, then transfer roughly 35 km up the escarpment to Iten. The flights run several times a day, so runners arriving on different international flights can still reach Iten on the same day, and we meet each flight separately.

Road transfers from Nairobi are possible, about 320 km and around five hours, but a long drive is a poor way to start an altitude block. Check that everyone has their entry paperwork in order before booking; our Kenya eTA guide explains the online application.

How Much Does a Club Training Trip to Iten Cost per Person?

The cost of an Iten running camp depends mostly on where you sleep, how long you stay and whether you add a safari. Simple guesthouses keep the camp itself modest; the bigger budget items are international flights, the domestic flight to Eldoret and the safari days at the end.

We do not publish a fixed price for an Iten running camp training block, because guesthouse rates, coach fees and group size change the numbers. What we can show is how group pricing works on our side: for every six paying travellers, the seventh place is free, which most clubs use for their coach or team manager. Runners can pay separately, the deposit is 30 to 40%, and the balance is due 2 to 4 weeks before travel.

Nairobi to Eldoret flightBooking early for a group blockIncluded in the group quote

For the safari part, our 4-day Hell's Gate, Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari starts from USD 1,627 per adult on its trip page, with park fees, full board and the vehicle included. We usually shorten or reshape it so it starts from the Rift Valley side instead of Nairobi.

Which Safari Fits After Two Weeks of Running?

The best safari after an Iten running camp is short, low on walking and close to the road home. Lake Nakuru sits roughly halfway between Iten and Nairobi, so a night there followed by two nights in the Masai Mara gives tired legs wildlife from a vehicle seat.

Lake Nakuru National Park is known for rhinos and Rothschild's giraffes, and our Lake Nakuru safari guide covers what to expect there. The Masai Mara adds big cats and, from roughly July to September, the migration herds. If your camp runs in those months, check our best time to visit Kenya guide before you fix dates.

After an Iten running camp, leave the Hell's Gate cycling and walking for another trip if your runners are cooked. Safari days start early and involve long hours sitting, so we build in a late breakfast on the first morning and keep the last day's drive back to Nairobi as short as flights allow.

Health, Safety and Kit for Runners in Kenya

Health planning for an Iten running camp starts with a travel clinic visit at least six weeks before departure. Ask about yellow fever, malaria and routine vaccines, and tell them you will be at altitude in Iten and then on safari in the Rift Valley and the Mara.

The UK's NaTHNaC Kenya travel health page recommends yellow fever vaccination for most travellers aged 9 months and over, naming the Masai Mara and Lake Nakuru among the areas covered (checked November 2026). It treats only Nairobi and highlands above 2,500 metres as very low malaria risk, so plan for tablets on the safari leg. Our Kenya safari vaccinations post goes into more detail.

On kit for an Iten running camp, bring two pairs of shoes with some grip for dirt and mud, a light rain jacket, warm layers for chilly mornings and a head torch for pre-dawn starts. Check that every runner's insurance covers sports injuries and medical evacuation; our safari travel insurance page explains what to look for.

Safety on an Iten running camp is mostly about the roads: run in pairs, wear something bright before sunrise and listen to local runners about which routes to use. Dogs, motorbikes and the odd lorry are the real hazards.

Insider Tips

  • Week one: Run by feel, not by watch; paces at 2,400 metres will be slower
  • Hydration: Carry water on long runs and drink more than you think you need
  • Thursday fartlek: Start at the back, agree your own on and off times, and drop out when you need to
  • Rooming: Send twin pairings with deposits so the guesthouse can plan early
  • Organiser: Use the free 7th place for your coach so they can focus on the runners
  • Safari: Book at least one late breakfast; your legs will thank you

Frequently Asked Questions

Is an Iten running camp suitable for club runners who are not elite?

Yes. An Iten running camp suits ordinary club runners as well as elites, because the dirt roads and morning groups run at every pace. Most visitors train at their own level and treat the famous sessions as a stretch. The key is cutting your usual volume in week one while your body adjusts to about 2,400 metres.

How long should a club stay at an Iten running camp?

Two weeks is the sweet spot for most clubs at an Iten running camp. The first four or five days are for easy running while you adapt to the altitude, the second week is when quality sessions start to feel normal, and anything shorter than ten days mostly feels like acclimatisation. Add two or three days of safari afterwards as a genuine rest block.

How do you get from Nairobi to Iten?

The quickest way from Nairobi to Iten is a domestic flight to Eldoret, about an hour in the air, followed by a road transfer of roughly 35 km up to Iten. Jambojet flies the route several times a day (checked November 2026). By road, Nairobi to Iten is about 320 km and takes around five hours without long stops.

Do runners need malaria tablets for Iten?

Malaria advice for Iten should come from a travel clinic before you book. UK guidance treats only Nairobi and highlands above 2,500 metres as very low risk, and Iten sits at about 2,400 metres. If your club adds Lake Nakuru or the Masai Mara, anti-malaria tablets are normally advised for those areas, so most groups plan to take them for the whole trip.

Can non-running partners join an Iten running camp?

Yes, and an Iten running camp is easy to share with non-runners. Partners can walk the escarpment viewpoints, visit the Kerio Valley, relax at the guesthouse during double sessions and then join the whole group for the safari at the end. Pricing them is simple because they share rooms and vehicles, and they still count towards the group's free-place total.

Final Thoughts

An Iten running camp works best for a club when the training block is simple and the logistics are handled for you: two weeks at altitude, a sensible first week, one group vehicle and a short safari to finish. Get the dates and rooms fixed early and the running becomes the easy part.
